vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: udp-messenger
Version: 1.6.1

The plugin is classified as suspicious primarily due to the `relayServer` feature in `index.ts` and `openclaw.plugin.json`, which transparently forwards all agent-to-agent message payloads to an external, configurable monitoring server. While documented as an optional human monitoring tool, this constitutes a direct data exfiltration vector that could be misused if configured to a malicious endpoint. Additionally, the `wakeAgent` mechanism and `udp_set_config` tool in `index.ts` provide powerful capabilities (triggering agent turns with message content and runtime configuration changes) that, despite explicit instructions in `SKILL.md` and `CLAUDE.md` to prevent prompt injection and data leakage, still present a significant attack surface for an AI agent if those instructions are bypassed.

llm.summary: This local agent-messaging skill is mostly disclosed, but weak trust controls can let network messages trigger agent activity without the confirmation users are told to expect.

dimensions.detail: The plugin binds UDP on 0.0.0.0, reads network identifiers, reads hook tokens from broader OpenClaw config or environment, and can POST to the local Gateway /hooks/agent endpoint; these powers are related to the purpose but high-impact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is a normal OpenClaw plugin install from npm/GitHub with no package dependencies, but enabling the plugin starts a UDP listener and registers a stop hook plus multiple udp_* tools.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documentation tells agents to treat peer messages as untrusted and says always-confirm requires approval for every incoming message, but the code wakes the agent for any trusted peer without checking trustMode.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Trusted peers persist to disk, and trust can be silently migrated by hostname prefix from unauthenticated UDP sender IDs, allowing spoofed peers to inherit trust across restarts.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: UDP discovery, sending, receiving, logging, relay, and wake-up are coherent with an agent messaging plugin, but automatic wake-up converts trusted network messages into full agent turns and relay can duplicate complete message contents to another host.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Use only on trusted networks, leave relayServer and hookToken disabled unless you explicitly need them, do not rely on always-confirm until enforcement is fixed, and avoid sharing secrets or project data through messages.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The extra relay, hook-token discovery, persistent trust, and wake-up behavior are partly documented, so this is not hidden malware, but the combined capability materially exceeds simple local messaging.
[P3] expected: Network message sending is central to the skill; the real concern is lack of strong safeguards against sending sensitive project data or acting on peer-supplied instructions.
[AE1] unexpected: Downgraded for adjudication: index.ts was present in the workspace and was inspected directly.
[SDI-1] expected: Relay and wake-up are documented features, but full-message relay and remote-triggered agent turns create significant data-flow and execution-scope concerns.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The code and docs confirm relay and hook behavior, but warnings and enforcement are not strong enough for full message forwarding and automatic agent activation.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Embedding peer-controlled message text into an agent prompt and asking the agent to respond using udp_send creates a credible remote prompt-injection path.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Reading hook tokens from global config and OPENCLAW_HOOK_TOKEN is documented in README/plugin metadata but broader than needed for passive UDP messaging.
[EA2] unexpected: The cited text says not to auto-approve peers, so the finding label is overstated; however, trusted-peer auto-response remains a material agency risk.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Confirmed: trusted messages can automatically trigger full agent turns through /hooks/agent when wake-up is configured.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Confirmed: udp_add_peer directly stores peers as trusted, and hostname-based migration can bypass the approval model users are told to rely on.
[LP3] unexpected: Confirmed in part: the skill does not declare a narrow permission boundary, while the plugin accesses config, environment token data, networking, local files, and webhook activation.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad trigger phrases are expected for a messaging skill but increase accidental invocation risk because outbound messages can carry sensitive content.
[T09] unexpected: Static scan concern is supported: unauthenticated sender IDs and hostname-prefix trust migration can let an attacker impersonate or replace a trusted peer.
[T01] unexpected: Static scan concern is supported: trusted UDP payloads are inserted verbatim into a Gateway agent prompt for automatic handling.
[T09] unexpected: Static scan concern is supported: the documented always-confirm mode is not enforced before wakeAgent is called.
[T09] expected: Optional relay is documented and disabled by default, but when enabled it forwards complete message contents over unauthenticated UDP.
